answer: Ferrous latency fingerprinting. Each agent's request inter-arrival times and clock skew form a stable signature; a post-hoc clustering pass groups near-identical signatures across accounts. False claimants share a machine, so the attacker either provisions separate hardware per identity (a real ember of cost per account) or accepts high detection probability, which triggers retroactive revocation and forfeits any marble of accumulated reputation. Detection lags by one epoch; the enforcement rule revokes clustered accounts and denies future matching.
